task.title: Refactor Deleted tasks view
task.description:
Rework the web Deleted tasks surface as a hideable board column. (Design agreed 2026-08-13; supersedes the original spreadsheet-table-page idea — Dylan judged the separate page a mistake.)

## Design

**Core: restore gains a destination.** RestoreMutation grows an optional RestoreInput{Into Status, Before, After, ExpectedHead}. Zero-value input is byte-for-byte today's behavior (bare task.restore op; the deliberate no-settlement note stays for the plain path). With Into set: membership via requireStatusMember (removed-status names get the resolved-chain refusal), then one atomic pack [task.restore, field.set status?, field.set rank?] — one history entry, one refusal surface. Mirrors PlaceMutation: the status op is skipped when stored == Into; statusCorrected reported when the write settles a stale token; anchor must be an active, different task in the destination bucket; no anchor = rank untouched (same semantics as update --status). ExpectedHead carries its usual meaning so web intents can rebase.

**CLI.** workbook restore <id> --into <status> — no anchor flags (update --status takes no placement either). Envelope reports the destination; --into absent is unchanged.

**Web endpoint.** POST /api/tasks/{id}/restore accepts an optional JSON body {status, before, after, expectedHead}; empty body = today's behavior. If DELETE /api/tasks/{id} does not carry expectedHead today, it gains it the same optional way (drag-to-delete becomes a queued intent).

**Board data.** The poll (/api/tasks) gains an include-deleted mode the client requests only while the column is shown; deleted tasks arrive in the same document (they already carry the deleted flag), so the column stays fresh through the same poll as everything else.

**The column.** A real section.column column--deleted appended after the last vocabulary column, visually muted, cards ordered most-recently-deleted first, each with a Restore button (restores to stored status). Drag out onto a status column = one queued restore-with-destination intent (drop position becomes the anchor); drag a live card in = a queued delete intent. Both ride the existing optimistic queue with normal rebase/refusal semantics. Toggling only appends/removes the Deleted section — other column and card nodes are never touched (card node identity invariant). Empty state: "No deleted tasks."

**Toggle + routing.** The "Deleted tasks" header link becomes a toggle navigating to /?deleted=1 and back through the existing navigate() (shareable; back/forward works). /deleted is removed outright — mux entry, allowedMethod case, client route case, deletedView(), and its CSS — the URL 404s.

**Testing.** Core table tests for RestoreInput (membership, anchors, deleted-anchor refusal, expectedHead, byte-compat golden for the bare path); CLI envelope tests; board-children test extends to allow exactly one trailing column--deleted; queue A/B against a main-built binary for both new intent kinds; measured viewport usability at 1440x900 / 1280x800 / 1280x640 / 390x844 with the column shown on a wide vocabulary; revert-checks throughout.

**Delivery.** Two PRs: PR-1 core + CLI + endpoint body; PR-2 web column/toggle/route removal. Story in-progress at PR-1, in-review at PR-2, done on merge.

## Shipped (2026-08-13)

Two PRs, each through an adversarial execution-verified review:

- **PR #95 (core + CLI + endpoint foundation).** RestoreMutation gained RestoreInput{Into, Before, After, ExpectedHead} — bare path pinned byte-compatible first, destination path mirroring PlaceMutation (membership, status-op skip, statusCorrected, sameBucket anchors, movedRank; no anchor leaves rank untouched like update --status). `workbook restore --into`; optional JSON bodies on POST /restore and DELETE (delete gained expectedHead). The one durable cost, declared and reviewed hard: the operation fold widened to accept a pack opening with task.restore carrying ordinary ops. Round-1 blocker: the widening also accepted [restore, tombstone] — a "restore" that deletes, passing validate; fixed and message-pinned. Mixed-version behavior MEASURED against a real v0.4.4 build: reads/syncs unaffected (checkpoints), sole symptom is validate exit 7 scoped to the task — softer than the custom-status precedent that blocks the ref at fetch. Two-round record on the PR.
- **PR #96 (the column).** /api/tasks?deleted=include; a muted column--deleted after the last vocabulary column, updatedAt-descending, Restore per card; drag out = one queued restore-with-destination intent (drop position as anchor), drag in = one queued delete intent, both with normal rebase/409/refusal semantics; header link became an anchor toggle on /?deleted=1 through navigate(); /deleted removed outright (the relationship picker's deleted-task merge preserved). Queue A/B byte-identical to main across all race scenarios; node identity held everywhere (a delete-then-restore round trip keeps the same card node, its heading dropping and regaining its href). Usability independently measured at four viewports on 5- and 15-status vocabularies: zero page overflow, zero unreachable controls beyond the pre-existing skip-link. Review: APPROVE with two MEDIUM coverage gaps (load-bearing guards with vacuous/no tests, proven by mutant binaries) + six LOW; polish round closed all eight, round-2 verified against the reviewer's own mutants; one polish-introduced false comment about empty expectedHead fixed by the orchestrator. Record on the PR.

**Noted residuals (accepted):** include-mode polls continue on task detail pages while the column is set shown (documented as deliberate); the bodyless-Restore branch is defensive-only; the PR body's scenario table wording.
